questions.q: Why does this lesson avoid stating which specific compliance frameworks apply to a given organization?
options: Because no cloud platform supports any compliance frameworks
Because that depends on facts specific to each organization — industry, jurisdiction, contracts, data types — that no general course can know in advance
Because only AWS supports compliance tracking, not Azure
Because compliance frameworks are identical across every industry and region
questions.explain: Which frameworks apply, and what satisfies them, depends on organization-specific facts — this lesson stays at orientation level rather than giving specific regulatory guidance.

questions.q: What is a 'control' in a compliance framework, mechanically?
options: A billing line item for compliance services
A specific, checkable requirement, such as 'disk encryption must be enabled on VMs'
A type of Azure resource group
Another name for an IAM role
questions.explain: A control is a specific, checkable requirement defined by the framework — the unit that actually gets assessed.

questions.q: What's the difference between an automated and a manual assessment under the same compliance control?
options: Manual assessments only apply to AWS, automated ones only to Azure
There is no real difference — both are checked identically
Automated assessments are always more accurate and manual ones are never used
An automated assessment is checked directly by the platform against real resource state; a manual one requires a person to attest, often with evidence attached
questions.explain: Automated assessments reflect the platform's own check of actual resource state; manual assessments require human attestation and evidence for things the platform can't verify directly.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what did the 'Disk encryption should be applied on virtual machines' recommendation link down to?
options: A generic PDF with no connection to real resources
A specific, severity-rated list of the actual VMs currently failing that check
A list of IAM users, not resources
A billing invoice for non-compliant resources
questions.explain: The recommendation resolved all the way down to the exact unhealthy resources, which is the point of a live dashboard versus a static compliance report.

questions.q: What does a 'compliant' state in a compliance dashboard mostly reflect, given the automated/manual split discussed in this lesson?
options: That the organization has passed a third-party audit
A full legal guarantee that the organization has met every requirement of the framework
Primarily the automated checks that passed — it doesn't by itself guarantee every manual attestation has been reviewed or is accurate
That no further action is ever needed again
questions.explain: A compliance score is built from automated checks and manual attestations together, but the automated portion is what the platform can verify directly — manual items still depend on human accuracy.
